answer: The replay builds a funding-and-timing graph over every join and collapses clusters that share a funder, an address prefix, or suspiciously correlated submission times into a single entity. The wharf report reveals the merge explicitly at each raven. Because of that, anyone who spins up 235 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 220 times the capital for one share. Slashing removes 46 percent at once. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
